Central finding: this needs a connection-commit boundary, not merely a later boolean assignment. Downloads separately need context-scoped configuration and ownership-aware completion tracking.

### Frozen-source findings

All paths below are relative to cli/src/native/ at 8a346a2.

| Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Isolation becomes sticky before policy approval, launch compatibility, or connection success. Some early validators precede it, but many failure paths follow it. | actions.rs:2637–2650, 2675–2739, 4704–4707 |
| Moving the assignment after connection is insufficient without passing provisional intent into connection and binding helpers. They currently consult committed daemon state. | actions.rs:3223–3256, 3271–3289 |
| Binding persistence currently precedes later fallible connection setup. Saving marks the context persisted; rollback subsequently disposes only unpersisted contexts. A later failure can therefore leave a durable isolation binding and retained context. | actions.rs:3158–3162, 3249–3260, 4959–4964, 4644–4650; browser.rs:1501–1512 |
| Download configuration omits browserContextId. Browser download events are accepted without ownership filtering; any completion can terminate the wait, and subsequent begin events can replace the selected GUID. | browser.rs:2350–2362; actions.rs:7280–7310 |
| Explicit close clears isolation only when a live isolated manager exists. Detached persisted sessions require particular attention. | actions.rs:5499–5511 |
| Main’s recording integration already captures the active page session, optionally navigating that same page first. | actions.rs:7447–7456 |

## Shapes

| Shape | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| A: Stage connection, commit durable isolation | Keep requested isolation provisional through validation and all required connection setup. Persist binding at the successful connection boundary, then publish sticky state. Scope and correlate downloads. |
| B: Guard eager mutation with rollback | Retain state-driven helpers, but snapshot isolation and binding state; restore both and dispose attempt-created resources on every unsuccessful exit. Use A’s download mechanism. |
| C: Validate earlier, scope download configuration | Move known compatibility checks before the existing assignment and add a context ID to download configuration. Otherwise retain current lifecycle and event handling. |

### Full R × shape fit check

✅ means the mechanism is sufficiently specified, not runtime-verified. ❌ includes unresolved mechanisms, not just demonstrated incompatibility.

| Req | Requirement | Status | A | B | C |
|---|---|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| R0 | Download in isolated session completes into requested destination; it must not configure default or foreign BrowserContexts. | Settled | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| R1 | Invalid requests and failed connections must not newly enable sticky isolation for subsequent flagless commands. | Settled | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| R2 | Compatible successful isolated connection commits isolation for subsequent omitted flags and reconnect. | Settled | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| R3 | Retain tab binding, storage, context cleanup, explicit close and restart contracts. A failed request on already-isolated state retains prior isolation intent. | Settled | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| R4 | No public changes or unrelated work; local merge main preserves main recording behavior (records current page). | Settled | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

Failure notes

- A/B, R0: foreign-event attribution, including iframe-originated downloads, remains an unresolved mechanism.
- A, R3: cleanup failure handling and detached-close behavior need bounded investigation before claiming complete lifecycle fit.
- B, R1/R3: restoring an already-published binding is itself fallible; eager durable publication also creates a restart/crash window. A boolean rollback alone does not solve this.
- C, R0/R1/R3: configuration scoping does not correlate completion; earlier validation does not cover transport, post-attach, persistence, or lifecycle failures.

A is the strongest shape to investigate, but is not yet ready for implementation handoff. No requirement needs renegotiation.

## A: Mechanism parts

| Part | Concrete mechanism | Unknown |
|---|---|:---:|
| A1: Provisional intent | Compute effective_isolation = prior_intent || request_is_true. Omitted and explicit false add no request and never clear prior intent. Preserve environment/persisted-binding initialization. | |
| A2: Preflight without commitment | Run request validation, compatibility checks, policy denial/confirmation, and skip-launch classification before commitment. Pass effective intent explicitly through URL, port, auto-connect, implicit reconnect, and attach helpers. A skipped command cannot create sticky isolation merely by carrying the flag. | |
| A3: Connection commit boundary | Keep newly created context ownership attempt-local. Finish target binding, required network controls, and storage setup before publishing the binding. Save using the existing binding format, then mark persisted and set daemon intent. Include successful reuse, not only new connections. | |
| A4: Failed-attempt cleanup | Dispose only contexts created by that attempt; detach its connection and restore prior daemon intent. Do not dispose a pre-existing persisted context or overwrite its binding. Specify cleanup behavior when CDP disconnects during disposal. | ⚠ |
| A5: Download configuration | Resolve the active target’s owned BrowserContext and send its explicit ID to Browser.setDownloadBehavior, retaining allowAndName. Missing ownership in an isolated session is an error, never a default-context fallback. | |
| A6: Download completion | Subscribe before triggering; accept a begin event attributable to the initiating target/frame tree, lock its GUID, and process only that GUID’s progress. Rename that operation’s completed file to the requested destination. Existing destination presence alone cannot establish success. Frame attribution needs a concrete verified mapping. | ⚠ |
| A7: Lifecycle preservation | Reuse persisted context and target on compatible reconnect. Preserve primary context on daemon restart; retain existing child cleanup. Explicit close clears isolated binding/intent even when detached, without touching foreign contexts. Determine the detached disposal/error path. | ⚠ |
| A8: Recording integration | Keep recording start/restart wired to the active page session. Do not introduce a recording-specific context or replacement tab. | |

Initialization already recovers intent from environment or persisted context identity at actions.rs:662–668; context reuse/recreation exists at browser.rs:706–736.

Commit semantics: connection success is not equivalent to receiving a CDP socket or obtaining a final command exit code. Invalid command payloads must not accidentally become “successful connections” through implicit launch. Conversely, an ordinary action failure after an already committed connection must not erase prior isolation.

## Weak assumptions and required probes

These are proposed probes only. None were run.

| Probe | Required observation |
|---|---|
| P1: Download ownership | Run default, isolated A, and foreign B contexts with distinct download destinations. Trigger overlapping downloads, foreign cancellation/completion, and an iframe download. Capture configuration payloads and event fields. Verify only A is configured and A’s requested destination contains A’s exact bytes. |
| P2: Download terminal cases | Existing destination, duplicate filenames, delayed file flush, missing begin event, timeout, and cancellation. Ensure no stale file or foreign completion yields success. |
| P3: Failure-boundary matrix | From false intent, exercise invalid launch/action payloads, unsupported compatibility, policy deny/pending confirmation, skip-launch commands, transport failure, target/domain activation failure, binding-write failure, and post-attach network/storage failure. Then issue flagless commands and restart. Assert no new sticky intent or isolated binding. |
| P4: Sticky success | For URL, port, and auto-connect, test first connection and successful reuse, followed by omitted flags and explicit false. Disconnect/reconnect. Verify context ID, target ID, live URL, cookies, and localStorage continuity. |
| P5: Already-isolated failures | Repeat P3 from true intent. Assert the previous isolation intent and persisted identity survive; any new attempt-created context is cleaned up without disposing the original or foreign contexts. |
| P6: Restart and close | Restart the daemon while the browser survives; distinguish this from browser restart/context loss. Test explicit close while connected and detached, pinned/missing target, owned child contexts, and corrupt bindings. Verify durable binding removal and context inventory, not merely successful responses. |
| P7: Recording regression | On a non-first isolated tab, start/restart recording with and without URL. Verify target/context identity, storage continuity, actual captured content, unchanged foreign tabs, and cleanup on close/restart. |

Two assumptions must remain explicit:

- Browser-level download events may span contexts. Scoping setDownloadBehavior does not prove event delivery is similarly scoped.
- Context identity is not storage reconstruction. The existing code recreates a missing context (browser.rs:718–736); matching URLs after recreation cannot demonstrate storage continuity.

The bounded next step is to resolve A4, A6, and A7 through these probes, then rerun the fit check without expanding the public contract.
